thread:
Samir (Docs): i've opened a docs PR to tighten up the metering header examples and clarify dashboard vs billing units. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/461
Leah (Eng): thanks. quick question — do we cite the exact telemetry field? runtime exports `redwood_token_count_total` in metrics, but our ingestion maps it to `redwood.token_count`. we should be explicit which name goes in the PromQL snippets vs the docs' JSON/SDK examples.
Mike (Billing): correct mapping: metrics -> `redwood_token_count_total`, ingestion/tag -> `redwood.token_count`. historically we had an alias `tokens_v1` for a short window; customers might see duplicates if charts combine both sources.
Samir (Docs): good to know. i'll include a short "migration note" explaining the alias period. also planning to add a small numeric example in the Pricing page so people can follow the math.
Zara (Analytics): also note that visualizations normalize by time (we show token-seconds to compare bursts). that can confuse folks when they try to compute invoice amounts if they assume the chart numbers are the billed units.
Samir (Docs): draft copy: "Charts use token-seconds for burst-normalized visualization; invoices charge on raw token units (token_count). For cost calculations, aggregate token_count across the billing period." ok to use that?
Mike (Billing): yes. can you add an explicit arithmetic example with numbers? makes it concrete.
Samir (Docs): adding example now:
```
# Billing example (monthly)
monthly_tokens = 2_400_000
price_per_1k_tokens = 0.10  # USD per 1k tokens
cost_usd = (monthly_tokens / 1000) * price_per_1k_tokens
# => (2400000 / 1000) * 0.10 = $240
```
Samir (Docs): i'll also show a short PromQL snippet for the dashboard panel and the ingestion field for the analytics runbook.
Leah (Eng): for header examples, the runtime emits `x-redwood-usage: tokens=789; model="rw-2.1"; customer="acct-123"`. include both the raw header and an SDK example (python + curl) so it's easy to replicate for infra and customers.
Samir (Docs): proposed curl + python snippets:
```bash
curl -H 'x-redwood-usage: tokens=789; model="rw-2.1"' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
```python
headers = {"x-redwood-usage": 'tokens=789; model="rw-2.1"'}
resp = client.generate(prompt, headers=headers)
```
Samir (Docs): also adding PromQL for the panel: `sum(rate(redwood_token_count_total[5m])) by (model, customer_id)` — will paste into the dashboard docs.
Zara (Analytics): please reference the 5m rate window in the text and mention that the panel uses sum over customer_id to avoid per-model noise.
Samir (Docs): done. one more question: how should we call out embeddings billing? some customers ask whether embedding calls count as tokens.
Mike (Billing): embeddings are billed as `embedding_units`, separate from token_count. add a single-line note linking to the pricing table and the embeddings section.
Samir (Docs): added. migration note draft: "If you observe duplicated token counts between 2024-12-02 and 2024-12-09, this was due to a short-lived alias during pipeline change; prefer `redwood.token_count` for billing and `token-seconds` only for visual burst charts." good?
Leah (Eng): lgtm. tiny nit: use lowercase header name `x-redwood-usage` in examples for consistency. also include semicolon spacing variants so ops can grep examples.
Zara (Analytics): approve from analytics side — added the PromQL line and clarified the panel title text in the doc.
Mike (Billing): approve pricing language. suggestion: use term "billing period" rather than "billing window" to match invoices.
Samir (Docs): updated per feedback and pushed a new commit. tagging @Leah @Zara @Mike for quick thumbs.
